html:
SMTO-GWT-0055 — SMTO couldn't connect to the Gateway

GUID: 9ad1b0a7-6d26-4497-9d27-6db02f542b1f
Slug: gateway-connect-failed
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • Connecting to the Gateway failed for a network reason SMTO couldn't pin down. This request was not sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for this Gateway. A fresh check shows whether the problem was brief or is still happening.
  2. If it fails, select the Gateway's name to expand it and read the Last check message, then select Edit and confirm Scheme, Host and Port. The Last check message often names the actual network problem that this error couldn't.
  3. Make sure the Gateway computer is on, and that both computers are connected to the network (VPN on if your setup needs one). Most connection failures come from one of the two computers being offline or off the right network.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows the Gateway as connected, and your request runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Last check message, to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't delete and re-add the Gateway; that won't fix a network problem. Check whether any interrupted earlier step already finished before repeating it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Connecting to the selected inbound Gateway raised an OSError that did not match the DNS, refused, unreachable, timeout or TLS categories, before the request was sent; no narrower cause is known.

What this means

  • An OSError during connection establishment did not match the narrower DNS, refused, unreachable, timeout or TLS categories. This connection failure occurs before application request transmission. That boundary applies to this request and does not settle any previous operation.

Why this can happen

  • An OSError during connection establishment did not match the narrower DNS, refused, unreachable, timeout or TLS categories.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the bounded connection diagnostic and selected endpoint; retain the unknown narrower cause unless additional evidence supports it.

How to fix it

  • Read the underlying OSError (errno and message) for this connection in the Server log, verify the Gateway record's Scheme, Host and Port, and run Check connection to see the Gateway's current health. Repair only what that detail identifies; don't change unrelated settings on a guess.
  • Check the retained connection detail, configured endpoint and intended Gateway health; repair only the prerequisite the evidence identifies.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected route connects and verifies without relying on an invented cause.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • This connection failure occurs before application request transmission. That boundary applies to this request and does not settle any previous operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
